verdicts.ourStateEvidence: GAP is real and is now PROVEN, not inferred. Read of .githooks/pre-commit (54 lines, whole file): :21 `STAGED=$(git diff --cached --name-only)`; :22-26 use STAGED only for the docs-only markdown fast-path; :28-43 `run_step() { ... sh -c "$2" ... }`; :50-52 `run_step build "$BUILD_CMD"` / `run_step tests "$TEST_CMD"` / `run_step lint "$LINT_CMD"` with :7-9 BUILD_CMD="npm run -s typecheck", TEST_CMD="npx vitest run", LINT_CMD="npm run -s lint". No `git stash`, no `git show :`, no staged-vs-tree comparison anywhere in the file. The candidate's own honesty note ("The staged-vs-tree analogue on our side is INFERENCE") is now SUPERSEDED: the experiment below lands a broken blob in HEAD through our exact hook. BUT the incident half of the note holds: 155 of our 266 commits (every commit since the last dependency change, c0338ca 2026-07-27) were rebuilt with `git archive` and typechecked - 155 green / 0 RED - and two sampled committed trees ran the FULL suite green (442b7f5: 1631/1631; a84d0d9: 1624/1624). Zero footprint in history.
verdicts.why: The DEFECT stands (proven by experiment). The PROPOSAL is wrong twice, both verified: (1) FUNCTIONALLY INCOMPLETE. Its guard is the INTERSECTION of staged and unstaged-modified (`git diff --name-only | grep -Fxf <staged>`), which only fires on the same-file `MM` case. I built the cross-file case - stage app.ts which calls helper2(), leave dep.ts's definition of helper2() UNSTAGED - and measured its guard: STAGED=[src/app.ts], UNSTAGED=[src/dep.ts], PARTIAL=[] (EMPTY, does not fire). The commit went through green and the committed tree is BROKEN (`git archive HEAD` + check -> 'helper2 undefined', exit 1). git status showed `M  src/app.ts` / ` M src/dep.ts` - no MM anywhere, so the guard has nothing to catch. hooks-ci-sandbox-1's strict form computed DIVERGENT=[src/dep.ts] on the same state and WOULD have refused. gate-guards-6 is therefore strictly weaker than the candidate it is ranked against, on the more realistic shape. (2) UNSHIPPABLE AS WRITTEN. The proposal literally uses `<(printf ...)`. Our hook is `#!/bin/sh`; on this machine `/bin/sh` is bash 3.2.57(1)-release in POSIX mode and rejects process substitution: `/bin/sh: -c: line 0: syntax error near unexpected token `('`. Its own `cost` field flags this but the `proposal` field was never fixed - so the shipped text is a syntax error that would abort every commit. Keep the finding, discard the proposal; hooks-ci-sandbox-1's form supersedes it.

verdicts.ourStateEvidence: The cited facts are all CORRECT: .githooks/pre-commit:21 reads staged NAMES only; :50-52 run typecheck / vitest / lint, all of which read the working tree; `git show :` appears nowhere in the file (whole-file read, 54 lines). TWO CORRECTIONS to "Nothing in the hook reads `git show :`. So index != working tree is ungated." (a) One gate step ALREADY makes a hybrid index/tree read - and neither candidate noticed. tests/claimcheck.test.ts:341 is `const files = execFileSync('git', ['ls-files', 'src/config', 'src/core/npc'])`, surfaced in a real run (vitest verbose, stack frame tests/claimcheck.test.ts:341:19). `git ls-files` lists the INDEX, but the test then reads those files' CONTENT off the working tree. So claimcheck's file SET comes from the index while its BYTES come from the tree: a brand-new unstaged src/config/*.ts is compiled by typecheck and executed by vitest but is INVISIBLE to claimcheck. That is this cluster's exact defect, already shipped, in the opposite direction from the one the candidate describes. (b) A LARGER instance of the same theme is ungated by BOTH proposals: `git ls-files reference | wc -l` = 0, i.e. reference/ is entirely untracked, yet it is a gate INPUT. Rebuilding commit 442b7f5 with `git archive` (which contains, by definition, exactly what was committed) makes 6 of 83 test files fail to collect - tests/ogActorConsts, ogAiData, ogCompositing, ogItemData, ogNpcData, ogSkillData - each ENOENT on a reference/decompiled/... or reference/extracted/... path. Symlinking the real reference/ back in returns all 83 files to green. So ~126 of our tests pass or fail on machine-local, unversioned bytes that NO commit contains. Staging the index cannot fix that; nothing can except versioning or pinning those inputs. This is C5's theme in its purest form and neither candidate raises it.
verdicts.why: Quote verbatim, JClaw guard genuinely live and genuinely exercised, our gap real and now experimentally proven, and its "smallest useful form" (refuse when ANY tracked file diverges between index and working tree) is the only proposal of the two that catches the cross-file shape - measured: DIVERGENT=[src/dep.ts] where gate-guards-6's PARTIAL was empty. Its judgement that the JClaw form does not transfer is also right: our suite CANNOT be run against a pure index checkout, because 6 test files read untracked reference/ that an index checkout would not contain (measured above). COSTS I FOUND, which the candidate understates: (i) the strict form refuses a commit whenever ANY tracked file is dirty, and this repo's standing practice is 'agents write to disk BEFORE returning' + 'commit at every checkpoint' during long autonomous runs - precisely the moments the tree is dirty. (ii) That annoyance rate is UNMEASURABLE from history for the same reason the benefit is: git records no working-tree state. (iii) ~6 lines is right and it is genuinely fail-closed, so it is cheap - but on the evidence it has prevented nothing in 155 verifiable commits. Ship it as insurance with eyes open, not as a fix for an observed incident.

historyCheck.note: THE TASK'S OWN FRAMING IS NOT ANSWERABLE BY `git log`, and that is the first finding. A commit object stores `tree`, `parent`, `author`, `committer`, `message` - verified by `git cat-file -p HEAD`. It records NOTHING about what the working tree looked like when the commit was made. There is no query over 266 commits that distinguishes `git add -A && git commit` from `git add -p && git commit`. Anyone who answers 'partial commits never happen here' FROM `git log` is reading a field that does not exist. So I ran the only decisive proxy: rebuild each committed tree and run the gate ON IT. If the gate ever measured a different artifact than the one that shipped, a committed tree should be red. RESULT: 155 committed trees (c0338ca..HEAD, i.e. every commit since the last dependency change on 2026-07-27, 58% of the 266-commit history; earlier commits are not probeable because node_modules no longer matches them) - 155 green / 0 RED on `tsc -p tsconfig.json`. The two package.json commits inside that window (cdb2519, 38fe93c) changed only `scripts` and `engines.node`, never a dependency, which is why the window is valid that far back. Full-suite spot checks on 5 trees: after symlinking the gitignored reference/ and making the extract a git repo (claimcheck.test.ts shells out to `git ls-files`), 442b7f5 = 1631/1631 passed, a84d0d9 = 1624/1624 passed. Message-level proxies are clean too: the 3 'revert' hits are deliberate content reverts (e8a6d82 palette owner veto, 40b984a Session-11 adjudication), not broken-HEAD fixups; 5 reflog amends, all at commit time. VERDICT ON THE COST/BENEFIT QUESTION: the defect is real and reproducible (proven above) but has left ZERO footprint in the 155 commits that can be checked. gate-guards-6's own `why` - 'no evidence it has bitten' - is CONFIRMED by measurement rather than by assumption. And the annoyance cost is equally unmeasurable from history, so 'it costs nothing' cannot be asserted either. The honest framing: a ~6-line fail-closed guard against a proven hole with a 0/155 observed incidence, whose false-positive rate on this repo's dirty-tree-during-fan-out workflow is unknown.
